children: , the server and enterprise-infrastructure supplier, added another AI chip option to its hardware lineup as Axelera AI's Europa accelerator became available in selected Dell systems, Reuters reported. Dell shares jumped approximately 4.7% to $568.86, based on the latest quoted price shown in the chart.

Europa is built for a different corner of the AI boom. Axelera says the processor can deliver 629 trillion operations per second while operating at a 45-watt thermal-design limit, equal to roughly 14 TOPS per watt. That makes the chip more relevant for power-conscious enterprise inference than heavyweight AI training. Reuters also reported that Axelera is targeting $1.5 billion in potential sales, though the company made clear that figure represents pipeline opportunities rather than booked orders or recognized revenue.

Dell already has serious AI momentum behind it, shipping $16.4 billion of AI servers last quarter and ending the period with a $95 billion backlog. That backlog is roughly 5.8 times one quarter of AI-server shipments, although it says nothing about the timing of future revenue recognition. The chart adds a valuation warning: Dell's $568.86 share price stands 148.68% above its GF Value estimate of $228.75, suggesting investors are already paying heavily for the AI infrastructure growth story.

title: Dell Jumps 4.7% as a 45-Watt Inference Option Joins Its Racks
